High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.785/2022 dated 10.12.2022 registered at Police Station Shahpur, District Betul for an offence punishable under Sections 420, 409, 34 of IPC.
Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is in custody since 21.01.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tampering with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
This bail application has been argued on the ground that there were no allegations against the applicant in the initial FIR.
He was falsely implicated on the basis of statements given by co-accused Mahesh Shukla.

It has been claimed that an amount of Rs.5,60,000/- was defalcated through applicant, but in his memorandum of statements applicant has disclosed that he received only Rs.3,000/- in account and only Rs.500/- was paid to him on every financial transaction.

sentences.text: In this case an amount of almost Rs.70,00,000/- was embezzled under Pradhan Mantri Aawas Yojna and it is not material what share the applicant received in this embezzled amount.
His involvement is prima-facie shown in the crime as it was the financial scam, therefore, no favourable assumption can be made in favour of applicant for the reason that he was not named in the FIR.
It also needs to be mentioned here that the ground that applicant was not named in FIR was absolutely false as his name is very much mentioned therein as accused No.5.
It has been proposed by the counsel for the applicant that applicant may deposit some amount if this Court imposes any such condition.
In view of the act of the applicant and the gravity of crime, this Court does not find it appropriate to allow this bail application subject to any condition of depositing the amount.
Accordingly, this bail application is dismissed.
